canonical_statement: The study aimed to investigate the types and causes of drug-related problems and assess their severity in hospitalised Parkinson's disease patients in neurology wards.
The study used a retrospective design in the neurology department of a 1900-bed tertiary public general teaching hospital in China.
Eligible patients had idiopathic Parkinson's disease diagnosed by a neurology specialist according to the cited Chinese diagnostic criteria and took at least one anti-Parkinson medication daily.

population.label: Eligibility population
inclusion_criteria: Idiopathic Parkinson's disease diagnosed by a neurology specialist fulfilling the cited diagnostic criteria
At least one anti-Parkinson medication taken daily

canonical_statement: Patients were excluded for atypical parkinsonian syndromes or secondary parkinsonism, uncertain diagnosis, hospitalisation under 48 hours, or missing relevant data.

population.label: Eligibility population
exclusion_criteria: Atypical parkinsonian syndromes or secondary parkinsonism

canonical_statement: A Raosoft calculation indicated a minimum sample of 197 patients for 95% confidence, 5% margin of error, and 50% response distribution.
Demographic and clinical data were retrieved by pharmacist authors from electronic medical records and the hospital information system.
Drug-related problems were categorised with Pharmaceutical Care Network Europe classification version 8.03.
Drug-related problems were identified by neurology-trained clinical pharmacists and confirmed by a neurology specialist physician.
Because pharmacists did not provide medication appraisal to prescribers or directly contact patients, the PCNE cause domains Dispensing, Drug use process, and Patient related were excluded.
Drug-related problems were identified by comparing treatment with cited standard guideline recommendations and updated drug references.
Drug-related problem severity was classified with the NCC MERP index; two pharmacists independently performed DRP and severity assessments and resolved discrepancies through discussion.

Analyses used SPSS 20, separate patient-level and problem-level analyses, chi-square or Fisher exact tests for categorical variables, t tests for continuous variables, Mann-Whitney U for mean age, two-tailed alpha 0.05.
The analysis included 209 hospitalised patients with idiopathic Parkinson's disease.

canonical_statement: The retrospective medical-record design may introduce bias and may underestimate drug-related problems because physician and patient perceptions were unavailable.
Parkinson's disease severity and adherence to medication schedules were difficult to obtain, and missing data may cause selection bias.
The single-hospital sample from 2017-2018 was relatively small, limiting generalisability to the wider population of China.
Only part of the PCNE classification was used to assess drug-related problems.
The authors concluded that drug-related problems occurred at high frequency among hospitalised Parkinson's disease patients.
The authors concluded that Parkinson's disease patients were more likely to be non-adherent to medications, particularly levodopa preparations.
The authors proposed that enhanced prevention, management, and pharmacist identification of drug-related problems could improve care for hospitalised Parkinson's disease patients.
